title: How access policy rules use segment groups
aliases: segment group in access policy rule

prose.text: This subject covers how access policy rules refer to segment groups.

prose.label: Choosing a group or a segment.
prose.text: Rules use segments for individual applications and groups for shared access: [[zpa.policy.criteria:application-segments-criterion]]. {{new-member-extends-rule}}

prose.label: Boolean logic.
prose.text: Groups are joined by an implicit OR, and segments and groups by an explicit OR: [[zpa.policy.conditions:segments-or]], [[zpa.policy.conditions:segment-or-group-or]]. {{criterion-checks-segment-or-group}} Other criteria are joined by AND: [[zpa.policy.conditions:criteria-and]].

prose.label: Rename and disable.
prose.text: {{rename-effects}} The effect of disabling a group is open {{gap:enabled-false-effect}}.

Rule order and first-match evaluation are in [[zpa.policy.evaluation-order]]. The policy types the provider scans on group delete are in [[zpa.terraform.policy-rule-writes:cleanup-rewrites-rule-from-converter]]. Membership is in [[zpa.segment-groups.membership]].

checks.do: Whether a rule names the segment group, the application segment or both, and whether other criteria in the rule are joined by AND.
Whether the group's enabled flag is false when a rule that names it appears not to match.
Whether a lookup by group name still resolves after a rename, since rules hold the ID.

operand-holds-id.statement: A policy rule refers to a segment group by ID: a v1 operand is `APP_GROUP` with `lhs` `id` and the group ID as `rhs`, and a v2 operand is `APP_GROUP` with the group ID in `values`.

quotes: // Check if Values array contains the segment group ID

criterion-checks-segment-or-group.statement: A rule's application criterion is satisfied when the requested application segment, or the segment group that holds it, is one the rule names.
criterion-checks-segment-or-group.conditions: Chain of evidence: the help describes the check as 'an application segment OR its segment group are present'; this restates it as the match condition.

new-member-extends-rule.statement: A segment added to a group named in a rule falls under that rule through its group, without the rule being edited.
new-member-extends-rule.conditions: Chain of evidence: the criterion checks the segment's group, so a new member satisfies it. The service's handling of the new membership is not stated.

rename-effects.statement: Renaming a segment group leaves policy rules unchanged because they hold its ID, while a lookup by name, such as the SDK `GetByName` or a Terraform data source by name, must use the new name.
rename-effects.conditions: Chain of evidence: operands hold the ID (operand-holds-id) and the SDK name lookup compares the name. Rule behavior after a rename was not exercised.

enabled-false-effect.title: The policy-evaluation effect of enabled = false on a segment group
enabled-false-effect.blocks: using the enabled flag on a group as an access-control switch
enabled-false-effect.detail: The model carries enabled as a meaningful boolean and the console shows a Status of enabled or disabled, but no source states whether a disabled group stops matching in rules or is ignored. Unverified legacy statement: disabling takes all member segments out of policy scope at once. Create a rule on a group, set enabled to false and test a member's access in a non-production tenant.
